The power of attorney issued to the authorised representative of the joint tenderers must be valid until the fulfilment of the public contract. A tender is confidential until the decision to declare the tender successful is made. Tender value The tenderer submits the value of the tender in the PPR on the award criteria and assessed indicators page. Assessment of tenders The Contracting Authority assesses the tenders that have been declared admissible in accordance with the award criteria set out in Annex 2 to the Procurement Documents. The Contracting Authority awards the public contract on the basis of the tender that is economically most advantageous, considering the best possible value for money. If only one tender has been declared suitable in the public procurement, the Contracting Authority has the right to automatically award the maximum merit points to the tender and the tender will not be substantively assessed. STATEMENT OF WORK C. 1. OVERVIEW/BACKGROUND. The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. NLS requires additional DA2 units, consistent with the existing inventory

The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats.
